title: Can you look like Guts from Berserk in real life?
summary: He presents his original 4-day Guts training program, modelled on the Golden Age arc physique of Berserk: big torso, arms, neck and upper back with average legs. It's a gentleman split built on supersets and giant sets, with neck, abs and upper back trained every session, meant only for lifters who already have years of training.
claims: Aim for Guts' Golden Age arc physique; other arcs are too unrealistic or imbalanced
Guts went from slightly above average to massive in about 3 years; it may take you twice as long, but the result is still achievable with work
The program is too fatiguing for untrained muscles; first spend at least two years on a novice program like his Adam or Baki programs
Guts spent about 7 years building his body before the Golden Age arc
Kentaro Miura understood anatomy well, so Guts' transformation is more realistic than people think; the Golden Age physique is achievable naturally
Best physiques come from doing the same exercises for years and relying on progressive overload, as Guts kept swinging his sword with added weight
Run it as a 4-day gentleman split with an upper-body focus, since Guts has a big torso and arms on average-looking legs
Leave 48 hours between sessions except the last two days, which are back to back; two days are pure upper body and two mix upper and lower
A thick neck is a priority to resemble Guts; train it every session and hit every angle (flexion, extension), not just one motion
Heavy pullovers expand the ribcage, hitting the chest, triceps, shoulders and lats; Guts has a big ribcage
Pick weighted chin-ups if you're advanced and unweighted supinated inverse rows otherwise
Train abs every session if you want to look like Guts; any ab exercise works
Forearms matter for the Guts look and get direct finger-curl work several times a week
Alternate barbell rows and deadlifts week to week; if you do both, deadlift first, though he doesn't recommend it
Pick the second exercise based on the first: after rows do good mornings, after deadlifts do weighted pull-ups; higher-capacity lifters can do both
A plus means superset; several exercises in a row are a giant set with no rest in between
Guts has massive biceps, so direct biceps work is included
Calisthenics and weight options are interchangeable; there are many ways to reach the same physique
Legs are trained but not a priority; leg day is largely an excuse to hit the upper back too
Alternate deadlifts with Zercher/SSB squats weekly; only deadlifting creates imbalances because you never train knee flexion
Saturday pullovers are light pump sets for blood flow and recovery, since heavy pullovers come on Monday
Training the upper back every session builds the biggest upper back, not heavy deadlifts every 15 days
Causality is the law of cause and effect: become the master of the cause and you control the effect
exercises: main chest, triceps, shoulders press on Monday
4x8-12 heavy on Monday; 3xAMRAP light for pump on Saturday
chest, triceps, lats and ribcage expansion
3x6-8, or inverse rows AMRAP if less advanced
3x12-20 / 4x10-12; any flexion or extension, vary angles
as long as possible; abs every session
the day's one compound for chest and triceps
lots of core and upper back; prevents imbalances from deadlift-only training
